points.description: Uses a valid method: for each of the three triangles PAB, PBC, PCA, P lies on one of three loci (perpendicular bisector of a side, or a circle centered at one vertex of that side through the other), and finds the candidate points by intersecting these loci. Every step must be mathematically valid. Points are counted without double counting, and degenerate cases (P collinear with two of A, B, C, or P equal to a vertex) are excluded.

levels.says: Sets up the loci or casework correctly but the enumeration is incomplete or contains an invalid step.

points.description: Final answer is 17, supported by a valid count. Answers other than 17 earn nothing. 17 with no justification or with invalid steps does not earn the method mark.

rubric.notes: The solution earns full marks only if every step is valid and the final answer is 17. Part credit goes to a correct locus or casework setup with an incomplete count. A wrong final answer earns at most the method mark, and only if the steps shown are valid.
rubric.answer_key: Final answer: 17. The triangle is isosceles with AB = AC and apex angle A = 20°. For each of the triangles PAB, PBC, PCA, P lies on the perpendicular bisector of one side or on a circle centered at one endpoint of that side through the other endpoint. Intersecting these loci, removing degenerate points (collinear with two vertices, or coinciding with a vertex), and merging duplicates gives 17 distinct points. Checking uses cos 80° ≈ 0.17 to decide which intersections coincide or exist.
